headline: Approved $1,674.40 lump-sum payment to Alex Nicoll, up to $350 for an LPD gift, and a $360 data-line contract with Mobile Citizen.
summary: A search committee for a new library director was formed. Revised bylaws were adopted by a 5-1 vote. Cash payments will be rounded up to eliminate pennies, and a vote on suspending late fees for CDs, DVDs, and other materials is set for the next meeting.
decisions: Approved a $1,674.40 lump sum payment to Alex Nicoll, 6-0.
Approved rounding up cash payments to eliminate pennies, 6-0.
Approved the consent agenda, including the August 20 and September 3, 2026 minutes, 6-0.
Formed a search committee for the library director position, 6-0.
Adopted the revised Board of Trustees bylaws, with the MOU added, 5-1.
Approved up to $350 for Magna-Tiles and book plates honoring LPD, 6-0.
Approved spending $360 from the Machinery & Equipment budget line for Mobile Citizen data lines, 6-0.
Accepted several unanticipated donations under RSA 202-A:4-c and 202-A:4-d, 6-0.
Board consensus to explore options with DPW for a library dumpster.
Postponed approval of job postings until the next meeting.

plain_text:
Leach Library Board of Trustees 
Draft Meeting minutes 
September 30, 2026 at 7:00 PM 
Leach Library, Londonderry NH 
 
Members Present: 
 Nancy Hendricks, Chair 
 Beth Marrocco, Vice-Chair 
 Erica Laue, Secretary 
 Moira Ryan, Trustee 
 Azra Palo, Treasurer 
 Maryam Mallick, Trustee 
 Donna Plante, Interim Library Director 
Members Absent: 
 Jan McLaughlin, Trustee 
Call to Order: made by Chair Hendricks at 6:31 PM. 
Nonpublic Session: Motion made by Secretary Laue to enter nonpublic session under 
RSA 91-A:3, II(a), seconded by Vice Chair Marrocco. Motion passes 6-0 by roll call vote. 
Discussion points: 
 Alexandria Nicoll’s annual review has come due, and she has been recommended for a 
3.5% merit increase as a lump sum payment of $1674.40 due to her excellent 
performance and high level of involvement at the library. 
 Motion by Secretary Laue to approve the lump sum payment of $1,674.40 to Alex 
Nicoll, seconded by Trustee Mallick. Motion passes 6-0. 
Nonpublic session ended by roll call vote at 6:42 PM. 
No business conducted between the end of nonpublic session and the reopening of public 
session. 
Motion to reenter public session made by Secretary Laue at 6:59 PM, seconded by Vice 
Chair Marrocco. Motion passes 6-0. 
Consent Agenda: 
 August 20, 2026 minutes 
 September 3, 2026 minutes 
 Next meetings: 10/7, 10/21, 11/4 
 Motion to accept the consent agenda made by Secretary Laue, seconded by 
Trustee Mallick. Motion passes 6-0. 
Public Comment: None. 
Treasurer’s Report: presented by Treasurer Palo.
 $10,128.21 in the book account at the end of August 
 $43,017.43 in the trustee account at the end of August 
 We are still pending documentation of deposits that were not correctly documented. 
 A withdrawal has been made to refill the cash drawer now that we’re back in the building. 
Committee Reports: 
 We would like to reconvene the financial ad hoc committee to document and account for 
the donations made to the trustee account. 
Presentations and Discussion:  
 Building update: presented by Interim Director Plante. We are not done moving back into 
the building; there are still items in the Woodmont Conference Room of Town Hall that 
are being transferred. 
o Study Room B is not reopened to the public yet, as it is holding items that have 
not been returned to their original places. That is a work in progress. 
o We don’t have mold anymore, but we still have a humidity problem. ReArch and 
ENE will be helping us with monitoring and alerts for humidity peaks, and will 
provide us with a quote for temporarily using the boiler to control the humidity. 
One of the rental dehumidifiers started leaking, but ReArch should be able to 
replace or repair it for us. 
o ReArch also helped us dispose of the damaged furniture. Documentation has 
been completed. 
o No leaks were found after this weekend’s nor’easter! 
o The maintenance budget line will be above 80% expenditure for this fiscal year 
this month; we will likely have to overspend it. 
 Appreciation from the Trustees: Chair Hendricks would like to thank the community, 
particularly Bob Slater and Dave Walle, for supporting the library through its 
displacement. Interim Director Plante also thanks the Town Manager’s office for 
coordinating the initial relocation to LPD, and our contractors for going above and 
beyond so often. Thank you to LPD, the senior center, the historical society, the YMCA, 
LSD, Awesome CCG, the Friends, all the GMILCS libraries, and everyone else who 
stepped up for the library. 
 Fine-free request: Presented by Nick Maher-Lewis, Senior Circulation Librarian. 
o Nick would like the Board to consider permanently suspending late fees for CDs, 
DVDs, and other materials. There is research demonstrating that late fees reduce 
library engagement and increase patron guilt. We are one of two GMILCS 
libraries that still charge late fees. 
o We have saved more money repairing books than collecting fines from patrons, 
per data from 2023-2025. 
o Currently we don’t charge fines for books and audiobooks; we would expand it to 
include DVDs, CDs, and Library of Things. Materials that are missing for a certain 
period of time incur a replacement fee for the full cost of the item. If the item is 
returned, then that fee is waived. 
o Board discussion: late fees create additional barriers for patrons and prospective 
patrons who struggle to afford them. We will vote on this at our next meeting. 
 FY28 Staffing requests: presented by Interim Director Plante. The staffing requests that 
the Board considered were brought to the former Town Manager, who affirmed that it is 
the Board’s prerogative to advance them to the ballot as part of the budget instead of as 
warrant articles.
o Chair Hendricks: We will have the budget and the union contract on the budget in 
March 2027. There is concern about adding two more positions to it. 
o Treasurer Palo: If we advance them, it is more transparent to move them as 
warrant articles. Consider that a warrant article would have explicit votes by Town 
Council and the Budget Committee for voters to see on the ballot, which could 
increase support. 
o Secretary Laue: Support the positions, but concerns about the optics when we 
haven’t hired the children’s librarian position. 
o Vice Chair Marrocco: We could have someone hired to that position by March, as 
we move forward with hiring the new director. Part of the inspiration for the part-
time position is an increase in revenue for the library via the passport certification 
option. 
o Trustee Mallick: We need these positions, but there’s uncertainty. 
o Trustee Ryan: Support the warrant article path for March 2027. 
o Interim Director Plante: Do consider putting the full-time executive assistant into 
the budget, and holding off on the other position for now. Warrant articles add up 
in terms of voter fatigue, but the potential revenue stream of the executive 
position would justify putting it into the budget. There’s another GMILCs library 
that acts as a passport acceptance facility (Wadleigh in Milford) that earns 
$60,000 per year through that revenue stream, so the income could be 
substantial.  
 Secretary Laue: That allays a lot of concerns. 
 Chair Hendricks: Could we develop some sort of estimation of how much 
the position could potentially offset through this stream? 
 Vice Chair Marrocco: We should have a subcommittee to coordinate a 
campaign from the Board to communicate the Library’s budget requests 
and benefits to the community, ideally by January. 
 FY28 Warrant articles: presented by Interim Director Plante. 
o Town Council will be discussing warrant articles at their meeting on 10/19. For 
us, this involves the bond for Phase 2B of the building project and the union 
contract. We can also put articles on for capital gains and maintenance trust 
funds, if we have numbers and specific language for them. 
o Chair Hendricks: This is what Mr. Slater presented to us a few meetings ago. 
o Trustee Ryan: We don’t technically own this building, so the Board should clarify 
how the MOA affects it. 
o Interim Director Plante: Finance was not aware of the conversations between 
myself and the former Town Manager, so Justin Campo and Kim Bernard will be 
deciding what will be going forward to the Town Council on the 19th. If they are 
not, the Board will need to go directly to Town Council about it. 
 Remaining open positions: presented by Interim Director Plante. We have an open part-
time library page position, as well as the part-time children’s librarian position. Does the 
Board want to post them or wait until the new director is hired? The recommendation is 
to post the children’s librarian to start. 
o Board consensus is to review the postings at the next meeting before approving 
to post. 
Deliberations and Vote: 
 Adjusting replacement costs for pennies: presented by Interim Director Plante. Pennies 
are nonexistent, so the request is to change fees by rounding up or down for cash
payments. Motion by Secretary Laue to approve the rounding up of cash 
payments, seconded by Vice Chair Marrocco. Motion passes 6-0. 
 Library director search committee: We need one! Today is the last day that applications 
are open for the position, and we have six applicants. This should involve Board 
members, Library staff, members of the community, and should convene immediately.  
o Discussion around the benefits and drawbacks of having members of the public 
being part of the committee. Logistical concerns are significant. Trustee Ryan: 
what about having someone from the Friends? 
o Vice Chair Marrocco and Secretary Laue volunteer to be part of the search 
committee. 
o Motion by Secretary Laue to form a search committee for the library 
director position, to include two members of the Board, two members of 
the library staff, and one member of the Friends of the Library, the latter 
three to be identified by Interim Director Plante; seconded by Vice Chair 
Marrocco. Motion passes 6-0. 
 Board of Trustees bylaws draft: presented by Secretary Laue. 
o Interim Director Plante: recommend adding the MOA with the Town to the list of 
things new Trustees are provided. 
o Motion by Vice Chair Marrocco to adopt the revised bylaws, with the 
addition of the MOU, seconded by Secretary Laue. Motion passes 5-1. 
 Funding requests: 
o Honorary gift proposal: presented by Interim Director Plante. These are options 
for a thank-you gift to LPD for the use of their space during our reconstruction. 
They include 
 Gift cards for each staff member, up to a total of $450 
 Adding a Magna-Tiles police station set and book plates in honor of LPD, 
for up to $350 
 Prepare a gift basket of snacks etc., for up to $300 
 Motion to approve up to $350 for Magna-Tiles and book plates made 
by Secretary Laue, seconded by Treasurer Palo. Motion passes 6-0. 
 Contract: 
o Mobile Citizen, $360: presented by Interim Director Plante. Mobile Citizen 
supplies the data lines that are the hotspots in the building. This is paid out of the 
Machinery & Equipment line of the budget. Motion made by Secretary Laue to 
expend $360 from the Machinery & Equipment budget line, seconded by 
Trustee Mallick. Motion passes 6-0. 
 Acceptance of unanticipated funds under RSA 202-A:4-c and RSA 202-A:4-d: 
o Friends of the Leach Library: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum 2026-27 passes 
($225 value) 
o Patricia C. Ballard, on behalf of the Ballard family: $100 in memory of Marilyn 
Webster Ham 
o Debra Donovan: $100 in memory of Marilyn Webster Ham 
o Debra Donovan: two gift baskets worth $245, raffled off at the grand reopening 
o William M. Fox and Laura Maher-Swerchesky, on behalf of the West Running 
Brook Sunshine Fund: $50 in memory of Marilyn Webster Ham 
o Jane McDonald: $75 for the Children’s noon NYE party in December 
o Londonderry Historical Society: $100 to co-sponsor the September adult craft 
program 
o Motion made by Secretary Laue to accept these funds under RSA 202-A:4-c 
and RSA 202-A:4-d, seconded by Vice Chair Marrocco. Motion passes 6-0.
Public Comment: None. 
Additional Request: presented by Interim Director Plante. The cleaning company is requesting 
that we consider getting our own dumpster; currently we share the Town’s dumpster and the 
cleaners have to transport our trash there in their own vehicles. Board consensus is to explore 
options with DPW. 
Chair Hendricks makes a statement requesting that the Board give the Town Council some time 
to get their house in order. 
Adjournment: motion made by Secretary Laue at 8:12 PM, seconded by Trustee Mallick. 
Motion passes 6-0. 
Minutes prepared by Secretary Laue.
